newsitem.title: USA: Barshefsky favors long-term US, Canada wheat pact.
newsitem.headline: Barshefsky favors long-term US, Canada wheat pact.

text.p: U.S. Trade Representative nominee Charlene Barshefsky said on Wednesday a long-term agreement between the United States and Canada on Canadian wheat shipments coming into the U.S. would be in the best interests of both countries, and that she will work towards achieving that goal.

"I think if we could achieve a longer-term agreement with Canada, that would be in the best interests of both countries," Barshefsky told members of the Senate Finance Committee in her confirmation hearing.
In response to a question from North Dakota Democratic Senator Byron Dorgan, Barshefsky said she is concerned about a recent increase in Canadian wheat and barley shipments.

She said she has warned the Canadian trade minister that she would not tolerate any market disruption because of the increased shipments, and intends to talk again with the Canadians before a mid-March consultation on the issue.

"There's no question that Canadian wheat and barley shipments are right now running at what would be essentially record levels ... I have previously alerted the Canadian trade minister that we would not tolerate market disruptions here because of these excessive shipments," said Barshefsky.

"I intend to ask Canada formally for consultations at the six-month mark in our consultative agreement, which would be around mid March. I will, however, talk to the Canadians before that time," Barshefsky said.
Barshefsky said she does not "underestimate the difficulty" of trying to achieve a long-term wheat agreement with Canada, but said the consultations in March would be the first step.
